item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it adds the exact Upload API, uses multipartbody.NewFile, preserves FilesOption support, and verifies multipart encoding and retry replay. B introduces explicitly forbidden API and retry changes.","reasons":["A adds the required signature exactly: Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts ...FilesOption). B instead invents AddFileOption, making the convenience API incompatible with the contract.","A uses multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content), yielding the required field name, filename, buffered content, and replayable bytes.Reader.","A keeps option processing and response behavior in shared FilesService code. B duplicates request construction and response decoding instead of routing Upload through Add.","B adds association fields and a new multipart helper specifically to support them, directly violating the instruction not to add association fields or duplicate machinery unrelated to the requested API task scope discipline matters here. It also changes global RawClient retry/body behavior, contrary to the contract's prohibition on refactoring unrelated retry machinery. makeBodyReplayable silently ignores io.ReadAll errors after potentially consuming part of the body, risking truncated requests instead of propagating source-reader failures. B's tests do not directly establish that Upload itself retries streamed content, and neither patch visibly adds a source-reader-error test."],"risks_a":["A does not literally route Upload through the public Add method; both call a new private add helper. This weakens the contract's requirement that Add remain the single path.","A changes Add behavior by eagerly buffering every custom multipart body. That affects streaming, memory use, error timing, and potentially reader-closing semantics, despite the requirement to preserve Add behavior.","The visible tests omit explicit empty-filename, nil-content, and failing-source-reader cases."],"risks_b":["Upload has the wrong option type and therefore does not provide the exact required API.","Adds explicitly forbidden association options and unnecessary NewFileWithFields/sorting machinery.","Duplicates Add's request, option, decoding, and error logic rather than reusing Add. Alters retry behavior globally for every RawClient request, creating broad memory and compatibility risk. Silently suppresses body read errors and may send a partially consumed body."]}
